summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput runs, discuss continuous batching, concurrency targets, queueing behavior, and next steps for on-prem pilot. Decided to run additional high-concurrency tests, share traces, and look at dedicated pool pricing. Some transcription noise; security docs requested.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm alex park from Redwood, we got samira on the call too. um quick roll call
[00:12] Miguel: miguel here, miguel santos, head of ml at nimbusdocs
[00:17] Priya: priya raman, infra
[00:20] Lars: lars holm, cto
[00:23] Samira (Redwood SE): hi all, samira gupta, i'll be driving the throughput runs today
[00:30] Alex: cool, agenda — quick recap of last week's runs, look at continuous batching settings, discuss concurrency targets and queueing/backpressure, then agree next steps
[01:05] Miguel: quick note, we've been seeing high 95th latency spikes when bursty traffic hits, we want to push overall throughput without blowing p95
[01:22] Priya: current setup is a mixed host, we have a k8s cluster with g4-like nodes and a small redis for caching, our requests are around 1.2k tokens average, sometimes 2k
[01:40] Samira: ok thanks, so last week we ran three profiles: baseline single-request, small batch (batch size 8) and large batch (32) using hosted endpoints with prefix cache warmed for 10 minutes
[01:58] Alex: the spreadsheet link is in the notes (see: https://drive.redwood/testbench/nimbus-thru-20270108.csv) — please ping if link doesn't open
[02:10] Miguel: i couldn't load it earlier, maybe perms, will check
[02:20] Samira: baseline qps was 150 rps, average latency 120ms, p95 at 280ms, with batching we saw up to 420 rps but p95 went to 420–600ms depending on cold kv-cache
[02:38] Priya: when you say cold kv-cache, is that the prefix cache on the model runtime or our redis layer?
[02:45] Samira: model runtime prefix cache — the serving runtime keeps KV cache per host, warm cache reduced p95 by ~35%
[03:00] Miguel: our main concern is tail latency, not just token cost, because we have SLAs to meet
[03:12] Alex: totally, tradeoff is batching increases throughput but can add queuing latency; continuous batching tries to keep latency bounded by grouping compatible requests quickly
[03:28] Samira: we toggled continuous batching window from 5ms to 25ms, 5ms favored lower latency but lower throughput, 25ms pushed throughput but increased p95
[03:45] Lars: what's our desired concurrency target? we can add more workers but want to understand diminishing returns
[03:55] Samira: we tested concurrency values 2,4,8; on dedicated pool 8 gave linear improvement up to 2x throughput vs 2, but p95 started climbing past 8 for big prompts
[04:15] Priya: queueing/backpressure — do you have suggestion for request queue size and backpressure signals we can use at app layer?
[04:25] Samira: yes, recommend soft queue at app with timeouts at 200–400ms, and set max inflight per host to concurrency target; runtime can return 429s when queues exceed threshold to let client retry
[04:40] Miguel: hmmm 429s are ok but we'd prefer retries rather than user-facing errors; can the SDK do exponential backoff automatically?
[04:52] Alex: yes our SDK has retry/backoff pluggable, we can share code snippet
[05:00] Samira: also suggested warmup flows — prepopulate KV cache using representative prefixes during ramp-ups so cold-start p95 isn't seen in production
[05:15] Priya: we can run a small job to warm cache every deploy or by traffic pattern
[05:22] Miguel: can you run one more round with simulated real traces? last time synthetic load didn't capture our burstiness
[05:30] Samira: absolutely, if you can share a sample trace we'll replay it; prefer a 7-day sample with tokens and timestamps
[05:40] Miguel: will do, i'll drop it in the drive link
[05:46] Alex: quick question about quantization — does using int8 vs fp16 change queueing or just per-token latency?
[05:55] Samira: it's mainly per-token compute speed, quantization reduces per-token time and increases throughput, but memory and kv-cache behavior can vary; we'll include quantized run
[06:10] Priya: about dedicated vs hosted, what are the pricing tradeoffs and burst capacity if we go dedicated?
[06:20] Alex: dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p95 variance, cost is higher but with commit and burst options you can get headroom; i'll send pricing delta by monday
[06:35] Miguel: any compliance or logs we can forward to security team? they need audit logs and KMS usage notes
[06:45] Alex: yes we have SOC2 summary, audit log export options, and KMS/HSM integration docs — sharing after the call
[06:55] Samira: back to tuning, we suggest a plan: run 3 throughput tests with concurrency targets 4,8,16, with warm cache and with and without continuous-batch windows of 5/15/25ms
[07:10] Priya: for the queue sizing, we'll instrument our app with max inflight 100 and see; is that per-host or global?
[07:20] Samira: per-host inflight, so overall capacity scales with pool size; also recommend per-route quotas
[07:35] Miguel: we also want to measure token efficiency — cost per 1M tokens under each config
[07:45] Alex: good call, include token counts in the spreadsheet
[08:00] Samira: starting now i'll kick off a baseline run then a batched run, i'll narrate as it progresses (transcription may drift during long runs)
[08:15] (run noises, brief silence)
[20:12] Samira: ok run one completed, baseline throughput 160 rps, p95 290ms, small batch 340 rps p95 420ms, large batch 620 rps p95 760ms with cold cache
[20:35] Priya: those large batch p95 numbers are higher than expected but that's with cold cache
[20:40] Samira: yes when we warmed cache for 15 mins large batch p95 improved to 480ms and throughput stayed 600 rps
[20:50] Miguel: that's promising — main worry is when spikes cause cache thrash
[21:02] Samira: recommended TTL tuning and shard-affinity to keep popular prefixes hot on same host
[21:15] Alex: also, autoscaling policy recommendation — keep a buffer of 20% spare capacity to handle sudden bursts
[21:28] Lars: curious about multi-region routing if one region saturates — can we failover gracefully to another region's model variant?
[21:36] Samira: yes runtime supports model variant fallback and cross-region routing though there is an added latency; we can set routing policy by latency vs cost
[21:50] Miguel: any competitor features we should watch for? we evaluated anthro, vertex; replication vendors had different caching approaches
[22:05] Alex: we'll note differences, but main focus is making our POC stable
[22:15] Priya: quick nit — the SDK snippet for adaptive retry, can you paste in the slack channel?
[22:22] Alex: done, will post link
[22:30] Miguel: next steps recap?
[22:35] Alex: samira will run 3x tests with defined concurrency and batch windows; miguel will share traces; alex will send pricing and security docs; schedule next check-in for 2027-01-28 to review results
[22:55] Priya: ok thanks all, sounds good
[23:00] Lars: thanks
[23:05] Alex: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned
[23:10] (call ends) note: some timestamps may be off due to transcription sampling and intermittent noise
